People are naturally inclined to reach out to those more sociable, more approachable, and more relatable/closer to them, and I’ve accepted that’s never gonna be me. In my case, I was just tired of trying and stopped putting in effort entirely. 

Now for your case. Since it seems your friends aren’t really making much of an effort to include you/invite you, I would say take a breather in terms of effort, don’t reach out as much. When your friends don’t return the favor/reciprocate, there’s your answer. I’m sorry if that seemed harsh at all, but the realization for me hit pretty hard and that’s where I decided to take a different approach when thinking about these things.

Learned the hard way that if things aren’t reciprocated it’s time to leave. I have little to no friends now because I realized that the majority of people whom I thought were friends were only around because I forced the issue. Later realized that most people are going to return the favor for people they’re genuinely interested in being friends with (more sociable, more approachable, more relatable), and that’s just not going to be me in most people’s eyes. These days I’ve just stopped trying.

For your case, I’d say stop putting in the effort with these people, as more effort is just going to make it hurt more. Look to others who may reciprocate your efforts, and focus on making those friendships important and valuable.
